disclaimer.note: LUNAR ECHO is a hypothetical mission inspired by NASA research. Budget, duration, and requirement values are fictional gameplay values, not NASA plans or specifications.

missions.name: LUNAR ECHO
missions.subtitle: Far-Side Radio Observatory
missions.description: Deploy a low-frequency radio telescope inside a far-side crater, shielded from Earth's radio noise.
missions.background: The lunar far side is the most radio-quiet place in the inner Solar System. A crater-based observatory could observe the cosmic Dark Ages at frequencies blocked by Earth's ionosphere. This scenario is inspired by the NASA NIAC Lunar Crater Radio Telescope (LCRT) concept.

objectives.label: Deploy a functional radio antenna array
Observe in the ~4.7–47 MHz band (LCRT Phase II concept range)

requirements.label: Total cost within mission budget (incl. launch)
Spacecraft mass within launch vehicle capacity
Positive daytime power margin of at least 100 W
At least 12,000 Wh of energy storage for the lunar night
Landing site on the far side, shielded from Earth radio noise

constraints: No direct line of sight to Earth — relay communication required
Lunar night lasts ~14 Earth days; survive extreme cold
Antenna must be deployed robotically inside the crater
successCriteria: Observatory operational for at least 6 months
